name: John Caudwell
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: John Caudwell founded mobile phone retailer Phones 4u before selling his stake in 2006 and 2011.
Born into a working-class family, he and brother Brian first started selling mobile phones in 1987.
Six years later the brothers founded Singlepoint, a mobile service provider that was acquired by Vodafone in 2003 for $650 million.
Caudwell pumped his share of the money into Phones 4u, which grew into the U.K.'s largest independent mobile phone retailer.
Three years later he sold a majority stake to Providence Equity Partners for $2.8 billion and, in 2011, unloaded the remaining 25% for $272 million.
forbes_facts: Caudwell is dating Lithuanian cycling champion and former Olympian Modesta Vzesniauskaite.
In 2018 he was ordered to pay a former financial advisor nearly $645,000 for wrongful dismissal but claimed victory as she had sought $25.8 million.

name: Otto Philipp Braun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Otto Philipp Braun owns 23% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
His father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales. Revenues have grown to around $8 billion.
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
The first sixth-generation family member to work in the company and serve on its board, Otto Philipp stepped down in 2017.
His sister Anna Maria Braun, also a billionaire, is CEO of B. Braun.
forbes_facts: Before resigning, Otto Philipp was responsible for the company's Iberian Peninsula and Latin American regions.

name: Frank Fertitta III
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Frank Fertitta III and his brother, Lorenzo, made the bulk of their fortune through mixed martial arts promoter UFC.
The brothers bought UFC for $2 million in 2001; it sold to an investment group led by WME/IMG for $4 billion in 2016.
They sold their remaining stakes in UFC in August 2017 at a $5 billion valuation.
The Fertittas took their casino business, Red Rock Resorts, public in 2016. It was founded by their father.
They each pledged $7.5 million in 2016 to NYU's Stern School of Business for a scholarship for veterans.
forbes_facts: His daughter Kelley got married at a lavish wedding at Red Rock Resorts in September 2018 where Bruno Mars sang.
Frank and Lorenzo got hooked on martial arts after taking weekly lessons in their casino's basement. Soon after, they bought UFC.

name: Cao Longxiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Cao Longxiang chairs Hubei Jumpcan Pharmaceutical, one of China's largest drug companies, specializing in both western and traditional Chinese medicine.
Cao's son, Cao Fei, serves as the company's vice chairman.
The company went public in 2001 as Hubei Hongcheng General Machinery, before Cao took control in 2013; he now owns more than 60% of the company.
Cao was a manager at a cement factory before taking a job with Hubei and served in the Chinese military before entering the pharma business.

name: Richard LeFrak
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Richard LeFrak became CEO of the LeFrak Organization in 2003 when his father Sam died.
The father-son team transformed the business, which started in France in 1883, into one of the largest real estate developers in the New York area.
Holdings include LeFrak City - a 20-building, 5,000-unit apartment complex in Queens - and hundreds of acres across from Manhattan to Newport, N.J.
Known for apartments for moderate-income tenants in the areas around New York City, LeFrak has recently been expanding into luxury and new markets.
LeFrak's biggest bet right now is SoLe Mia, a 184-acre mixed used project he's developing in North Miami.
An owner of rent-stabilized apartments in New York, LeFrak took a hit in June 2019 when state lawmakers made it harder for landlords to raise rents.
forbes_facts: Sons Jamie and Harrison are being groomed to be the next generation of LeFraks to run the business.
A large investment portfolio includes stakes in customer relationship management startup Affinity, skincare brand Fig.1 and storage firm MakeSpace.

name: Bent Wilhelmsen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025)
forbes_bio: Bent Christian Wilhelmsen is heir to the family that co-founded and remains one of the largest shareholder in Royal Caribbean Cruise Line.
He co-owns the family business through Awas Holding, inherited after his father Arne Wilhelmsen's death in 2020.
He is a principal in Awas Holding, a private investment group focused on cruise, real estate, offshore and financial assets.
The group owns Linstow, a real estate company developing major projects in Norway and the Baltics.
Wilhelmsen is involved in steering the family's diversified holdings with a focus on long-term value creation.

name: Francois Feuillet
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Francois Feuillet led French motorhome maker Trigano for 39 years before stepping down as its chairman in 2020.
Started in 1935, Trigano first made camping equipment and then branched out to become a leader in European leisure vehicles.
Feuillet took the company public in 1998, and he and his family owns 58% of the business.
He previously worked in finance and had an auditing job at KPMG.
Feuillet and his wife Marie-Helene still serve on the board of Trigano.
forbes_facts: Trigano's subsidiaries include prominent European RV brands Adria and Chausson.

forbes_bio: Pierre van der Mersch, dubbed the Belgian Warren Buffett, controls investment company Brederode.
He began his career as a bank clerk in 1958, and in the 1980s began building his fortune by taking control of a series of publicly-traded shell companies.
His asset management style focuses on taking long positions in undervalued companies.

name: Ales Zavoral
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Ales Zavoral is a Czech billionaire who, in 1994, founded Alza.cz, the e-commerce giant based in Czechia that operates in Germany, Austria, Hungary, Slovakia and other parts of central Europe.
According to recently published book, Ales Zavoral started as a collector of cigarettes butts and sold them to drunken punk club goers.
Ales Zavoral started to make computers in college sold them out of his dorm.
forbes_facts: Zavoral is an avid basketball lover and experienced pilot, and he owns a small bio farm in Bohemia, Czechia.

name: Michael Ashcroft
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Ashcroft's fortune comes from buying and selling a number of companies, most notably home security giant ADT.
He purchased ADT in 1987 then flipped it to Tyco International in 1997 for $6.7 billion; proceeds from the sale still form the bulk of his fortune.
A longtime Conservative Party supporter, he served as deputy chairman from 2005 to 2010, and stepped down from the House of Lords in March 2015.
Ashcroft is also a major investor in Belize and previously served as the Belizean Ambassador to the United Nations from 1998 to 2000.
forbes_facts: In 2015 he released "Call Me Dave", a scathing unauthorized biography of Prime Minister David Cameron that included salacious allegations of drug use and snobbery.
He admitted his disappointment that Cameron didn't tap him for a high-ranking post, but insisted that the book -- and its uncorroborated claims -- was not revenge.
